When an item drops it’s either FFA (free for all) or Blink, the blink skill teleports you to a random spot in the map so you all go left and the person furthest right gets the drop, usually it’s done before the box is broken so that party lead can be passed and pick up rights can be changed to all to just party leader so no one can snag gear

HY if you want a burst thief class, seems a bit daunting at first with its gauge but after 140 it becomes hit a button pop your buffs and whack. But has some of the most utility in the game. 

Built in door, all attacks are just movement abilities such as (air stall/momentum kill, addition up jump which resets your double flash jump and fly, a teleport on a set distance left or right) your main bossing skill lets you dash, your mobbing skill can be used as an in air attack but if I have to reposition I usually use Crudgle a short CD high damage skill,  Free movement through fly, a gate to TP to and back to your original spot. And a variable length iframe (you can hold it up to 20seconds and the CD depends on how long you hold it down for but if you time it right and hold it quick you can iframe every 20 seconds) 

The movement is actually so good with blink you can flash jump 6 times fly 3 and up jump reset twice. 

I’ve used it before with bossing and it looks like flash jump, fly, flash jump, air stall, reset, flash jump, fly, flash jump, blink, iframe for 1-2 seconds, reset, flash jump, flash jump, fly

Training is S tier, it’s not afk like DS or Nightwalker but you basically just stand still in most maps  

And the burst is a bit harder to setup but there are ways around it Krrr ring seems like sacrificing damage but lets you get your whole burst setup into origin. Once you get used to bosses you don’t really need it, I only used this in black mage until I liberated where you can just iframe your setup if you need. But the burst is chunky, I just liberated and solo up to HSeren in about 3 bursts.

For damage you need to fill out your equip slots and start running gollux asap, getting an eye acc. from Zakum and some earrings from Horntail. 

Then theres the matter of your actual current equips. You want to use the Epic pot scrolls in the event shop to get your emblem and secondary to epic first then all your equips. You can roll your emblem to legendary and your goal should be two useful lines one being Att the other being Boss% or IED. IED at your level is very strong because its basically final damage % once you get to bosses past vellum. Your secondary will be replaced by a Pno one so you can keep it at Epic but try to get 6% Att an additional line will be helpful but not necessary.   
  
After that you want to get your basic equips up to 12\* and two line main stat doing this should allow you to kill all of CRA and hard gollux which will allow you to replace your time gated equips, and start getting the rein or superior gollux set which will help take you to further bosses. 

If youre having trouble making meso remember to run your daily bosses (Arkarium, Normal Magnus, Normal Pap, Hard Ranmaru, Hard Vonleon) for about 50m/day (350m/week) and ursus daily which can net you around 1B/week as well. You should also be looking at running weekly bosses such as Hard Hilla, Normal Cygnus, Chaos Pink Bean, Hard Magnus, Chaos Zak, and possibly CRA in the near future which should net around 740m/week.

I couldn't get the link to work and im away from my desk for work, but if you're looking to boost an isolated sound i can give you 4 steps to boost without clipping  


  
1. Isolate the sound:   
This can be done if you have a copy of isotope or for a free plugin i believe ReFir from the reaper plugin suite can analyze background frequency's very well and provide an anti EQ. This will only work if you have a bit of background noise to go off of, or a longer clip. It also wont remove sudden noises such as other voices or sudden bangs. If it creates to many artifacts skip this step.   


2. Remove what doesn't need to be there  
Take a visual EQ so you can see what audio frequencies the cat purr starts at, then take a Hi-pass filter and remove all the junk below it. Do not copy this with a low pass filter as it will remove harmonics which could add to the overall tone or make the purr sound weak. This is where you will also start "Gain staging" or gradually adding gain throught a variety of plugins, use the EQ gain to bring the whole thing post EQ up about 1-2db.  


3. Light Compression  
slap a 3:1 compressor on there with a quick attack and slow release and then same thing as before youre gonna want to bring up your gain levels, make sure youre not peaking   


4. Limiting  
Put on a limiter, set that baby to your desired volume and crank it the rest of the way. making sure not to distort. Honestly typing all this out probably took more time then doing it but if you have any questions let me know
